# Current CEO of OpenAI as of May 2026

As of May 2026, **Sam Altman is the CEO of OpenAI**. Multiple sources consistently confirm his continued leadership of the company throughout this period.

Altman has remained a central and highly visible figure in OpenAI's strategic direction. According to [3], he leads what is currently the world's most valuable privately owned company, having announced ambitious plans including $1 trillion in datacenter investments and aggressive expansion into industries such as e-commerce, healthcare, and entertainment. The Guardian profile describes 2026 as a pivotal "make-or-break year" for Altman personally, as OpenAI prepares for a potential IPO toward the end of 2026 at a projected $1 trillion valuation, despite the company remaining unprofitable and spending tens of billions annually [3].

Altman has also been at the forefront of OpenAI's strategic pivot toward enterprise customers. He personally told a room of editors that enterprise would be a top priority in 2026, framing it as an "application problem" the company needed to solve [1]. This shift comes as OpenAI's enterprise market share dropped from approximately 50% in 2023 to 27% by the end of 2025, with Anthropic capturing around 40% of the market [7].

While Altman's role as CEO remains stable, OpenAI has seen notable changes among other senior executives. Brad Lightcap, the former COO, was shifted into a special projects role reporting directly to Altman, and Chief Marketing Officer Kate Rouch and AGI development lead Fidji Simo both took medical leaves [6]. These internal restructuring moves have been framed as part of a broader effort to win larger enterprise business deals [7].

Altman has also significantly expanded OpenAI's political footprint, increasing the company's lobbying spending from $260,000 in 2023 to $2.99 million in 2025 [3]. In terms of competitive outlook, he has publicly downplayed Google's Gemini as an existential threat, characterizing it as one of several "code reds" the company has navigated [1].

In summary, Sam Altman continues to serve as CEO of OpenAI as of May 2026, steering the company through an ambitious and consequential period of growth and restructuring [1][2][3][6].
